role: count certificates through a power-size auxiliary variety (M1a regime): #V_p = main + error with main term ≫ error at every large prime
missing_theorem: A family of varieties V_p with a map to the ES certificates of p, all fibres of size ≍ p^δ, and an asymptotic #V_p(ℤ) = 𝔐(p) + O(p^{δ−η}) valid for every large prime p with 𝔐(p) ≫ p^δ. Since #V_p = Σ_cert |fibre| ≍ p^δ·R(p), 𝔐(p) must vanish at odd squares (T1) and so cannot be a product of local densities; the only T1-exact main term known is p^δ·M_BM(p), and the error bound then says R(p) ≥ ε·M_BM(p), i.e. H⁻_BM rescaled by p^δ.
status_ref: CONDITIONAL_ES Prop 2.3 / Remark 2.4 (B3 does not exclude high-multiplicity encodings, but the main term is still M·μ); FRONTIER §2.4 (H⁻_BM), §3 B5 (singular-series main terms are positive at m²), B2_ACROSS_FIELDS M1a row

role: group action on integral points (M3 homogeneity), Markoff/BGS-style orbit method

role: calibration only (disproof hygiene): rule out an Erdős-type covering obstruction to ES
missing_theorem: (Calibration, true in substance.) There is no finite set S of primes and class a mod M (with primes in it) such that every positive solution of 4/p for p ≡ a (mod M) is excluded by congruences modulo S. Reason: a covering obstruction is a local obstruction to the defining condition; ES certificates are divisor events whose local densities are positive at every non-square (BL Thm 1.8: U_n(ℤ_ℓ) ≠ ∅ and the BM set is non-empty for every n ≥ 2; SYNTHESIS_SPARKS9 Prop 2.2: some level 4 | t ≤ 4ℓ(n) has positive BM level density iff n is not a square). Erdős's covering acts on primality of many shifts, which is not ES's condition.

role: propagation between certificate configurations by one-parameter moves (BGS rotations)

The fixed-(u,v) move is the endpoint forest F_p (edge uv iff uv | p + u + v), which is a forest (each v > 1 has at most one smaller neighbour); fixed roots and the least-non-residue root fail infinitely often under Dickson, and comp(1) can have 8 vertices i.o. role: integral Hasse/BM principle for the fixed-p (u,B,C) family of affine conics over the C-line
missing_theorem: For every large prime p, the total space {(u,B,C) : (4uC−1)(4BC−1) = 4Cp+1} has an integral point when its integral BM set is non-empty. Each fibre is a SPLIT affine conic xy = 4Cp+1 with x ≡ y ≡ −1 (mod 4C): its integral points are divisors of one integer in one class (finite set, no strong approximation for a split torus), so the fibrewise principle is the tied divisor event and the total-space statement is (★) itself.
